
Suppose six observed variables are caused by 2 latent factors as seen in @fig-model. 
```{r}
#| label: fig-model
#| fig-cap: Structural Model with Standardized Loadings and Residual Variances
#| fig-height: 7
#| cache: true
m <- "
A =~ .7 * A_1 + .8 * A_2 + .9 * A_3
B =~ .6 * B_1 + .7 * B_2 + .8 * B_3
A ~~ .4 * B
"

tikz_array <- function(x, ...) {
  apply(x, 2, WJSmisc::prob_label, ...) %>%
    apply(1, paste, collapse = ",") %>%
    paste0("{", ., "}", collapse = ", ") %>%
    paste0("{", ., "}")
}

latex_data <- function(x, prefix = "", suffix = "", ...) {
  if (typeof(x) == "double" | typeof(x) == "integer") {
    x <- apply(x, c(1,2), WJSmisc::prob_label, ...)
  }
  x %>% 
    apply(c(1,2), \(d) paste0(prefix, d, suffix)) %>% 
    apply(1, paste0, collapse = "&") %>%
    paste0(collapse = "\\\\\n")
}

latex_array <- function(x,
                        includenames = TRUE,
                        env = "array",
                        labelcolor = "gray",
                        align = NULL,
                        left = NULL,
                        right = NULL,
                        prefix = NULL,
                        suffix = NULL,
                        ...) {
  if (is.null(align)) {
    newalign <- paste0(rep("c", ncol(x)), collapse = "")
  } else {
    newalign = align
  }
  if (is.null(left)) {
    left <- "\\left["
  } else {
    left <- paste0("\\left", left)
  }
  if (is.null(right)) {
    right <- "\\right]"
  } else {
    right <- paste0("\\right", right)
  }
  
  main_array <- paste0(left,"\\begin{", env, "}{", newalign, "}\n", latex_data(x, ...), "\n\\end{", env, "}", right)
  
  if (includenames) {
    bigalign <- ifelse(is.null(rownames(x)), "c}\n", "cc}\n &")
    output <- paste0("\\begin{array}{",bigalign)
    
    if (!is.null(colnames(x))) {
      col_header <- latex_data(matrix(colnames(x), nrow = 1))
      output <- paste0(output, " {\\color{",labelcolor,"}\\begin{array}{",newalign, "}",col_header, "\\end{array}}\\\\\n")
    }
    
    if (!is.null(rownames(x))) {
      row_header <- latex_data(matrix(rownames(x), ncol = 1), suffix = "\\hspace{-2ex}")
      output <- paste0(output, " {\\color{",labelcolor,"} \\begin{array}{c}",row_header, "\n\\end{array}} & ", main_array, "\n\\end{array}")
    }
    
    output
    
  } else {
    main_array
  }
}



ram <- sim_standardized_matrices(m)$RAM_matrices
lambda <- ram$A[1:6,c("A","B")]
phi <- ram$S[c("A","B"), c("A","B")]
theta <- ram$S[1:6,1:6]
R <- get_model_implied_correlations(m)

tikzload <- lambda %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column() %>% 
  separate(rowname, c(NA, "id")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-id) %>% 
  filter(value != 0) %>% 
  pivot_wider() %>%
  select(-id) 
tikzvar <- ram$S[1:6,1:6] %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column() %>% 
  separate(rowname, c("construct", "id")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-c(id, construct)) %>% 
  filter(value != 0) %>% 
  select(-name) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = construct) %>% 
  select(-id) %>% 
  tikz_array(accuracy = .01)

```


In what is called the RAM Model [Reticular Action Model\; @mcardleAlgebraicPropertiesReticular1984]^[*Reticular* refers to things shaped or arranged as a net or network.], there are two types of paths in @fig-model: *asymmetric paths* (straight single-headed arrows) and *symmetric paths* (curved double-headed arrows). The asymmetric paths represent causal influences of one variable on another. The symmetric paths represent variances if the paths covariances if they connect two variables and variances if they loop back to the same variable. Any omitted path in @fig-model is assumed to be zero. Thus, we can arrange all the path coefficients in two matrices **A** and **B**, as seen in @fig-ram.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ram
#| fig-cap: Asymmetric and Symmetric Standardized Path Coefficients
#| fig-height: 7
#| cache: true
ram$A |> 
  corrr::as_cordf(diagonal = 0) |> 
  corrr::stretch() |> 
  mutate(Matrix = "Asymmetric<br>Paths (**A**)") |> 
  rbind(
ram$S |> 
  corrr::as_cordf(diagonal = diag(ram$S)) |> 
  corrr::stretch() |> 
  mutate(Matrix = "Symmetric<br>Paths (**S**)")) |> 
  mutate(x = fct_inorder(ifelse(str_detect(x, "_"), paste0(str_replace(x, "_", "<sub>"), "</sub>") |> str_remove("_"), x)),
         y = fct_inorder(ifelse(str_detect(y, "_"), paste0(str_replace(y, "_", "<sub>"), "</sub>") |> str_remove("_"), y)) |> fct_rev()) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x,y)) + 
  geom_tile(aes(fill = r)) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = prob_label(r)), family = myfont, size = 16, size.unit = "pt") +
  theme_light(base_family = myfont, base_size = 20) +
  scale_x_discrete(NULL, expand = expansion(), position = "top") +
  scale_y_discrete(NULL, expand = expansion()) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white") +
  theme(axis.text.x.top = element_markdown(),
        axis.text.y.left = element_markdown(), 
        panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        strip.text.y = element_markdown(angle = 0, color = "gray40"),
        legend.position = "none", 
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white")) + 
  coord_fixed() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(Matrix), axes = "all")
```


# Model-Implied Correlations


Model in @fig-model implies a specific correlation matrix. As explained in @bokerReticularActionModel2018, the correlations among the observed and latent variables can be calculated like so:

$$\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \left(\bf{I-A}\right)^{-1}\bf{S}\left(\left(\bf{I-A}\right)^{-1}\right)'$$

$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$ is the correlation matrix of the observed and latent variables.[^1] $\bf{A}$ is the matrix of asymmetric paths, $\bf{S}$ is the matrix of symmetric paths, and $\bf{I}$ is an identity matrix compatible with $\bf{A}$.

```{r fig-corr, dev='ragg_png'}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 8
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Model-Implied Correlations Among Latent and Observed Variables
get_model_implied_correlations(m, latent = TRUE) %>% 
  corrr::as_cordf(1) %>% 
  corrr::stretch() %>% 
  mutate(x = str_replace(x, "_", "<sub>") %>%
           paste0("</sub>") |> fct_inorder(),
         y = str_replace(y, "_", "<sub>") %>%
           paste0("</sub>") %>% fct_inorder() %>% fct_rev()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x,y)) + 
  geom_tile(aes(fill = r)) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = WJSmisc::prob_label(r)), 
            size = 18 * .8, 
            size.unit = "pt", 
            family = myfont) + 
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", 
                      high = "royalblue", 
                      limits = c(0,1), 
                      labels = prob_label) + 
  scale_x_discrete(NULL, expand = expansion(), position = "top") + 
  scale_y_discrete(NULL, expand = expansion()) + 
  theme_minimal(18, myfont) + 
  theme(axis.text.x.top = element_markdown(), axis.text.y.left = element_markdown(), legend.text = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + 
  coord_equal()

```


[^1]: Actually it is the observed covariance matrix, but we will assume that all observed variables are standardized (mean = 0, sd = 1). In that case, $\Sigma$ is also standardized (i.e., a correlation matrix is a covariance matrix that consists of standardized variables).
